timeline.title: The name Punjab enters wider written use
timeline.detail: The Government of Punjab’s historical account notes the term in Tarikh-i-Sher Shah Suri (1580), while also tracing earlier references to the land of five rivers.

timeline.title: Punjab is annexed by the British East India Company
timeline.detail: Following the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the Treaty of Lahore and annexation brought the Punjab under Company rule.

timeline.title: Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Amritsar
timeline.detail: A defining event in the history of colonial Punjab and the wider anti-colonial movement.

timeline.title: Partition divides historic Punjab
timeline.detail: The Radcliffe Award was made public on 17 August. Partition caused mass displacement, violence, separation and long-term family loss.

timeline.title: Indus Waters Treaty
timeline.detail: The treaty assigned the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej for India's use and the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab for Pakistan's use.
timeline.source: Punjab Roots — River and water history
